advances: A cover and contact identity on one old minimal deepest-base face, including a nested-family upper comparison with frozen thresholds.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
Fix the prescribed own supergradient $g$ and set $\phi(z)=\max_{X\in C_z}[f(z,X)-g\cdot(X-y)]$. The maximum is attained by compactness. Concavity follows by combining the maximizing marks inside $C$, and $\phi(p)=f(p,y)$ by the own supergradient inequality. To obtain a full supporting slope even at boundary bases, use 7227bbfcd12ad3d2, which applies to the finite canonical hull and supplies a uniform inradius $r_0>0$ and Hausdorff-Lipschitz fibers. For two fibers at Hausdorff distance $\delta\le r_0/2$, contracting the first about its inball center by $1-\delta/r_0$ puts it inside the second. In fact the support value after contraction decreases in every unit direction by at least $\delta$. Apply the contraction to a maximizing mark in the first fiber. Monotonicity and homogeneity give a buffer value in the second at least $(1-\delta/r_0)^\kappa$ times the old one. Its change in the linear term is bounded by a constant times $\delta$ because the fibers are uniformly bounded. Since $1-(1-\delta/r_0)^\kappa=O(\delta)$ on this interval, and $f$ is bounded, $\phi$ decreases by at most a constant times $\delta$. Reverse the roles for the other bound. For $\delta>r_0/2$, boundedness of $\phi$ gives the same estimate after increasing the constant. Thus $\phi$ is Lipschitz on $B$.

For a Lipschitz constant $L_\phi$ of $\phi$ on $B$, the function $\inf_{z\in B}[-\phi(z)+L_\phi\|w-z\|]$ is a finite convex extension of $-\phi$ to $\operatorname{aff}B$. Convexity follows by combining candidate pairs, and agreement follows from the Lipschitz inequality and the choice $z=w$ on $B$. The negative of any subgradient of this finite convex extension at $p$ gives a supergradient $\alpha$ of $\phi$ on $B$. Its bound on $\phi$ gives the asserted full tangent with the prescribed $g$.

For the cap group, let $c_j=a_j\cdot p+u_j\cdot y-\varepsilon f(p,y)=c_q(a_j,u_j)$. The weighted buffered constraint margin at $(z,X)$ is
$$
\sum_j\rho_j[a_j\cdot z+u_j\cdot X-\varepsilon f(z,X)-c_j]
=\ell\cdot(z-p)+\varepsilon[f(p,y)+\alpha\cdot(z-p)+g\cdot(X-y)-f(z,X)].
$$
The bracket is nonnegative. At a feasible point of $D_{q,\varepsilon}$ every individual term on the left is nonpositive by the closed quantile-region theorem. In particular $\ell\cdot(z-p)\le0$ at all bases in $I$, hence on their hull. As $p$ is in the relative interior of its minimal face, this linear displacement vanishes on $F_p$. Over that face the weighted buffered constraint margin is nonnegative. Adding $\varepsilon f(z,X)$ proves the bound on the fixed cap margins throughout each fiber. At a feasible point over the face the weighted buffered margin must instead equal zero, and every individual term vanishes by positivity of the weights. Since $\varepsilon>0$, the tangent bracket also vanishes.

On $C_t$ over $F_p$, replacing $f$ by $f_t$ only increases the same weighted buffered margin, with the old thresholds kept fixed. At least one new buffered threshold at the tested point is at least the corresponding old $c_j$, so its new closed cap lies in the old mass-$q$ cap and has mass at most $q$ under the smaller fiber measures. Taking the infimum gives the upper bound.
statement:
Use the finite mixed family and buffer of the closed quantile-region theorem. Assume additionally that $f(z,X)=\mathcal F(C_z,X)$, where the nonnegative marked functional $\mathcal F$ is inclusion-monotone and is multiplied by $s^\kappa$ under any common homothety of the body and its mark with ratio $s>0$, for some $\kappa>0$. Then every own-fiber supergradient $g$ at $(p,y)$ has a finite full extension $(\alpha,g)$ satisfying
$$
f(z,X)\le f(p,y)+\alpha\cdot(z-p)+g\cdot(X-y)\qquad((z,X)\in C).
$$

Let $(p,y)\in S$ be a global buffered maximizer at $\varepsilon>0$ satisfying $y\in\operatorname{int}K_p$ and $\varepsilon f(p,y)<\operatorname{dist}(y,\partial K_p)$. Put $q=Q_\varepsilon$ and take any positive-weight group of right-quantile mass-$q$ caps with the balance $\sum_j\rho_j u_j=\varepsilon g$ of the finite active-cap balance theorem. Write $I$ for the bases of the sampled global maximizers and $F_p$ for the minimal face of $\operatorname{conv}I$ containing $p$. For any such full extension $(\alpha,g)$, the corrected vector $\ell=\sum_j\rho_j a_j-\varepsilon\alpha$ satisfies $\ell\cdot(z-p)\le0$ on $\operatorname{conv}I$ and vanishes in displacement from $p$ on $F_p$. For every $z\in F_p$ and $X\in C_z$, the weighted margin of the same fixed actual caps is at least $\varepsilon f(z,X)$. Thus these closed caps cover the whole fiber. At any $(z,X)\in D_{q,\varepsilon}$ over $F_p$, all their buffered quantile constraints are equalities, as is the displayed full tangent.

For a nested compatible smaller family on the same positive sampled bases, with updated buffer $f_t\le f$ on its canonical hull $C_t$, the old fixed cap thresholds give the upper bound $b_{\varepsilon,t}\le q$ on the part of $C_t$ over $F_p$.
title: A fixed actual cap group covers its deepest-base face
